output.subject: Your question about the letter on your personal loan
output.body:
Dear ⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_1⟧,

Thank you for getting in touch and for setting out your question so clearly. We have received your message.

You told us you received a letter saying your personal loan is "in default status." This surprised you because, as you mentioned, you have made every payment this year, though some were a few days late. You asked us to explain in plain English what "default status" means, whether it is different from being past due, and whether you owe anything extra.

These are fair questions. A letter like this can be worrying, especially when you have been keeping up with your payments, and we're sorry for the concern it has caused.

A specialist team is reviewing your message so that the answer you receive is accurate for your situation. They will respond within 10 business days with an explanation of the letter and an answer to whether any additional amount is owed.

In the meantime, if you receive any further letters about your loan or have anything else to add, please reply to this email and we will pass it on to the team.

Kind regards,
Customer Care, Meridian Harbor Bank
notes_for_analyst: Intake marked this as a question, not a complaint, but it is in ACKNOWLEDGE ONLY mode, so the draft does not explain what default means.
Confirm the loan's actual status: in default, past due, or current.
Check whether the default letter was sent correctly given the customer's payment history this year.
Confirm whether any late fees, charges or other amounts are owed, and how much.
Decide whether the customer needs a plain-English explanation of default versus past due in the final response.
The customer may be worried about their credit; decide whether to address possible credit reporting impact in the response.
Draft greets the customer as ⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_1⟧; confirm this matches the signer ⟦NAME_1⟧.
